notes:
The list has 38 stations, which matches the text's count of "thirty-eight lighthouses". 23 rows carry a *. Skerryvore shares Hynish's * through the { brace, which gives the 24 stations with returns that the text reports ("Twenty-four stations have sent in returns, and fourteen have either sent none..."). None of the rows has a number on the committee's map or a type (L.H. etc.), so number and type are null throughout. The coast is the section heading you gave, WEST COAST OF SCOTLAND. The three Isle of Man stations at the end (Point of Ayr, Douglas Head, Chickens Rock) are printed under it with no sub-heading of their own.

How I transcribed it:
- Fragments drop only the page indent at the start of each line; every other character is kept, including the spaces before the ditto mark on the Skerryvore line.
- For a keeper, I dropped the full stop that ends the row ("J. M'Gill." → "J. M'Gill"). In the light descriptions I kept the final full stop, because sometimes it is part of an abbreviation ("every min.", "rev. ½ m.").
- Rows that run onto a second line: Cape Wrath, Monach Island, Dhuheartach and Sound of Mull. In each, only the keeper's name is on the second line.

Hynish and Skerryvore:
- Hynish's row reads "*{Hynish, Skerryvore Signal Tower, Tyree; no lights.† William Crow." The * and { come before the name and the † comes after "no lights.", so I recorded its marks as "*{ †".
- The † goes with the footnote at lines 1287-1288: "This station included by mistake, but retained for convenience, bracketed with the next." Hynish is the shore signal station for Skerryvore, not a light. Its "character" is just "no lights.".
- I took "Skerryvore Signal Tower, Tyree" as Hynish's place. You could instead treat "Skerryvore Signal Tower" as a description of the station, with "Tyree" as the place.
- Skerryvore's keeper is a ditto mark ("), which I kept as printed. It stands for William Crow from the Hynish row above.

Same or similar keeper names (copied as printed, not resolved):
- "Charles Black" is the keeper at both Devaar (*) and Turnberry. This could be a printing slip or two different men.
- Ewings: "J. Ewing" at Dhuheartach, "John Ewing" at Skervuile and "Ralph Ewing" at Loch Ryan.
- Lairds named Laidlaw: "David Laidlaw" at Ardnamurchan and "R. Laidlaw" at Corsewall.

Spellings copied as printed, not corrected:
- "Island Glass" (usually Eilean Glas or Island Glass, Scalpay, Harris)
- "Rhu Stoir" (Stoer Head)
- "Rosshire"
- "Argyleshire"
- "Tyree" (Tiree)
- "Dhuheartach" (Dubh Artach)
- "Rhuvaal" (Ruvaal)
- "Skervuile"
- "Lochindaul" (Loch Indaal)
- "Devaar" (Davaar)
- "Chickens Rock" (no apostrophe)
- "Loch Eil" given as Corran Ferry's place (Corran is on Loch Linnhe)
- "Lismore Island, Oban"

Other things to know:
- Monach Island has no place after the name. Its character "same tower, upp. white fl., low. red, fixed." describes two lights in one tower.
- Stornoway and Pladda each have two lights. I kept "2 lights, ..." and "2 lights 8 yards apart, ..." inside the character text.
- Mull of Kintyre and Monach Island have no county or island printed, so their place is null.
- No keeper is printed for Ushenish, Barra Head, Lismore Island, Sanda or Chickens Rock. None of them has a *.
